Veo 3.1 pricing: what it costs per second, and where

Edited by Emmanuel Gonzalez

Some links on this page are affiliate links. Affiliate disclosure.

As of Nov 24, 2026, the cheapest Veo 3.1 rate we track is $0.06 per second for Veo 3.1 Fast at 720p on Higgsfield’s Ultra (annual) plan, not stated, estimated from credit plan and priced on a 4-second clip ($0.24 a clip), assuming every credit you pay for is used. That rate uses a Higgsfield Black Friday plan price that ends Nov 25, 2026, 7:00 PM ET (4:00 PM PT). The cheapest pay-as-you-go rate is $0.10 per second for veo3.1_fast (no audio) without audio on the Runway API, a published rate ($0.80 for an 8-second clip). Google no longer sells Veo 3.1 pay as you go: its Gemini API preview models were shut down Oct 22, 2026, and Google Cloud lists its current Veo 3.1 models as Provisioned Throughput or fixed quota only. In Google Flow, every account gets 50 free credits a day, enough for 5 720p Veo 3.1 Lite videos.

Last checked 2026-11-24. Google’s pages were read Nov 24, 2026, 8:19–8:21 PM ET (5:19–5:21 PM PT). Catalog rows use the date on each row.

Key takeaways

  • Cheapest if you use every credit. $0.06/s for Veo 3.1 Fast on Higgsfield, Ultra (annual), 720p, not stated, estimated from credit plan, checked Nov 24, 2026. It uses a Black Friday plan price that ends Nov 25, 2026, 7:00 PM ET (4:00 PM PT).
  • Cheapest pay as you go. $0.10/s for veo3.1_fast (no audio) without audio on the Runway API, or $0.15/s with audio, published rates checked Nov 24, 2026.
  • Full Veo 3.1, not Fast. From $0.15/s on Higgsfield, Ultra (annual), 720p, estimated from credit plan. By API, from $0.20/s without audio on fal or the Runway API, checked Nov 24, 2026.
  • Google direct. No pay-as-you-go Veo 3.1 is listed. The Gemini API preview models were shut down Oct 22, 2026, and Google Cloud’s Veo 3.1 models are Provisioned Throughput or fixed quota only, checked Nov 24, 2026.
  • Free in Google Flow. 50 free credits a day buy 5 720p Veo 3.1 Lite videos at 10 credits each. Flow retires Veo 3.1 Fast and Quality on December 5, 2026.

    What does Veo 3.1 with audio cost?

    Among rows whose seller states that the clip includes audio, the cheapest on Nov 24, 2026 is $0.15 per second for veo3.1_fast (audio) with audio on the Runway API, a published rate with resolution not listed: $0.75 for a 5-second clip or $1.20 for an 8-second clip. On pay-as-you-go APIs, full Veo 3.1 with audio is $0.40 per second on fal at 720p/1080p and on the Runway API, so an 8-second clip is $3.20. At 4K, the cheapest row is $0.3432 per second for Veo 3.1 4K w/audio on Magnific, plan tier Pro (annual), from credit plan, checked Nov 22, 2026, assuming every credit you pay for is used. Higgsfield’s Veo 3.1 rows do not state audio, so they are left out of this comparison.

    Can you pay Google directly for Veo 3.1?

    Not pay as you go. Google’s Gemini API deprecations page, read Nov 24, 2026, lists veo-3.1-generate-preview, veo-3.1-fast-generate-preview, and veo-3.1-lite-generate-preview as shut down on October 22, 2026, with gemini-omni-1.2-flash as the replacement, and the Gemini API pricing page no longer lists Veo. On Google Cloud’s Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, the model cards for Veo 3.1, Veo 3.1 Fast, and Veo 3.1 Lite list pay-as-you-go as not supported; they are offered through Provisioned Throughput or fixed quota, in the us-central1 region. Our last Gemini API Veo 3.1 rows, last checked Oct 23, 2026, are kept as discontinued and are not used in any ranking on this page.

    How much does Veo 3.1 cost in Google Flow?

    Google’s Flow help page, read Nov 24, 2026, says every account gets 50 Google Flow credits a day with or without a paid plan, and unused daily credits do not roll over. Veo 3.1 Lite makes 4-, 6-, or 8-second videos at 720p for 10 credits each, or 5 credits on Google AI Ultra plans, so the free daily credits cover 5 Lite videos. Google AI Plus adds 200 credits a month, Pro 1,000, Ultra $100 10,000, and Ultra $200 25,000. Google says accounts without a paid plan may not be able to generate videos during peak hours, roughly 9 AM–12 PM ET (6–9 AM PT). Credit costs are per generation, not per request, and one request can make two videos.

    Is Veo 3.1 Fast being retired?

    In Google Flow, yes. Google’s Flow help page, read Nov 24, 2026, says Veo 3.1 Fast and Veo 3.1 Quality will be retired on December 5, 2026, and points users to Omni Flash 1.2 or Veo 3.1 Lite. It also says Veo Extend was retired on November 5, 2026. On Google Cloud, the Veo 3.1 and Veo 3.1 Fast model cards list a retirement date of May 4, 2027 or later, and Veo 3.1 Lite is listed as Preview. The third-party rows above come from each seller’s own pricing page, and none of those rows has a retirement date, so each stays in the table until its seller’s page changes.

    How do we calculate this?

    Each dollar figure is a current price row, with the vendor page and the date that page was checked. A published rate is a dollars-per-second figure on that page, or an API credit count times the credit price the page states. A credit-plan figure is plan price ÷ credits × credits per clip ÷ seconds, and it assumes every credit you pay for is used. When the vendor marks that count with "~", "roughly", or "estimated", the row is labelled estimated from credit plan and is not a list price. A promo shows its end date when the vendor gave one. The full method is on the about page.
